cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Acknowledge the Disrespect
cards.instruction: Make someone apologize for the disrespect to your position, not merely for what happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. Your apology should mention interrupting the chair, not just spilling the tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. The trousers hold no office.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Chair.' Let's repair the title while we're here.

mechanism: A imitates a confident status cue incorrectly, then demands an apology specifically for disrespect to the position A has claimed.
confusable: Unlike ordinary offense, D51 requires a position-based apology; S04 supplies the mistaken claim or practice.
comparison: Meeting chair and spilled tea versus a training leader publicly contradicted.
seedUse: Preserve repair of an apology and audience timing; make misunderstanding causal.
